headline: Canada Protects 81,400 Hectares of Northern Ontario Forest
meta_description: Canada safeguards 81,400 hectares of northern Ontario taiga forest and peatlands, protecting wildlife habitat and 30 million tonnes of stored carbon.
summary_short: Canada is protecting an area 1.3 times the size of Toronto in northern Ontario, safeguarding at-risk wildlife and massive carbon reserves.
body:
Canada is protecting 81,400 hectares of northern Ontario taiga forest and peatlands—an area 1.3 times the size of Toronto—in a conservation move that shields critical wildlife habitat and locks away 30 million tonnes of stored carbon.

The protected region spans the taiga, the boreal forest ecosystem that stretches across Canada's north. Peatlands, which make up part of this landscape, are among Earth's most effective carbon reservoirs. By securing this land, Canada removes the threat of resource extraction and development that could release those carbon stores into the atmosphere.

The designation also safeguards habitat for species already facing pressure from habitat loss and climate change. The protection represents a tangible step toward both climate stability and biodiversity conservation—two interconnected challenges where action in one area strengthens outcomes in the other.
